newsitem.title: USA: NRC proposes $100,000 fine for ComEd.
newsitem.headline: NRC proposes $100,000 fine for ComEd.

text.p: The staff of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission Thursday proposed fining Commonwealth Edison Co, a unit of Unicom Corp, $100,000 for engineering violations at its Zion nuclear power plant.
The agency said the move follows a meeting with the utility earlier this month to discuss an incident February 21 involving improper control rod movements at Zion's Unit 1.
Both reactors at Zion are currently shut down, the NRC said. ComEd is expected to discuss its findings on the incident and its corrective actions before either unit is restarted, the agency said.

The NRC said an inspection in July and August found several engineering violations at the plant involving failures to conduct safety evaluations, follow procedures, test systems and equipment or take prompt corrective action when equipment repeatedly malfunctioned.
NRC inspectors also found several instances where safety-related equipment was altered or the required safety evaluations were inadequate.
Commonwealth Edison has until April 11 to either pay or protest the fine. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
